newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails Euro response to Iran court decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails Euro response to Iran court decision.

text.p: The White House said on Friday it believed Germany and the European Union acted appropriately in responding to a German court's decision that Iran was responsible for killing four dissidents.
A Berlin court on Thursday ruled Iran's "political leadership" ordered the September 1992 killing of four exiled Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
In response Germany expelled four Iranian diplomats and the European Union moved to recall ambassadors and break off "critical dialogue" with Iran.
"We felt that the court decision was quite significant in confirming our long-held belief that Iran is a sponsor of terrorism," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry.

"The European Union and the German government responded appropriately to that court decision. We'll continue our very close consultations with our European allies about the activities that we deem reprehensible by the government of Iran," he said.
